There is no safe recovery path for mid-event interruption under strict append-only semantics.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the system supports an 'abort marker' that can be appended after a partial event to tombstone it, resumption could proceed by appending a fresh event after the abort marker.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If events are byte-stream fragments rather than atomic records, partial writes are normal and resumption is always safe.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"An event in the log must be atomically committed: it has a beginning marker, content, an end marker, and a predecessor hash. If the token budget runs out between the beginning and end markers, the log contains a partial record. Any resumption faces a dilemma: (a) append a new event referencing the partial one\u2014invalid because the partial event has no stable identity/hash; (b) rewrite the partial event to completion\u2014violates append-only. Both paths corrupt identity, so refusal is the only responsible action.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
